en/fa01-03-02.spoken: A computer has no eyes like ours. How can we give it a picture?
en/fa01-03-02.previousCheck: Transcript inspected against spoken line, including numeric values and terminology.

en/fa01-03-03.spoken: Divide the picture into little squares, and keep just one color in each square.
en/fa01-03-03.previousCheck: Transcript inspected against spoken line, including numeric values and terminology.

en/fa01-03-04.spoken: Make it simpler still: write one for black, and zero for white.
en/fa01-03-04.previousCheck: Transcript inspected against spoken line, including numeric values and terminology.

en/fa01-03-05.spoken: Read a row of numbers aloud. Let your child color the squares to match.
en/fa01-03-05.previousCheck: Transcript inspected against spoken line, including numeric values and terminology.

en/fa01-03-06.spoken: Keep the picture a secret for a moment. See when your child recognizes it.
en/fa01-03-06.previousCheck: Transcript inspected against spoken line, including numeric values and terminology.

en/fa01-03-07.spoken: Now try this cat. Here is the photograph before we turn it into squares.
en/fa01-03-07.previousCheck: Transcript inspected against spoken line, including numeric values and terminology.

en/fa01-03-08.spoken: As the squares get bigger, the fur and whiskers become harder to make out.
en/fa01-03-08.previousCheck: Transcript inspected against spoken line, including numeric values and terminology.

en/fa01-03-09.spoken: Eventually there are only eight rows left. Can you still spot the cat's ears?
en/fa01-03-09.previousCheck: Transcript inspected against spoken line, including numeric values and terminology.

en/fa01-03-10.spoken: Each row has eight zeros and ones. That fits neatly inside one byte.
en/fa01-03-10.previousCheck: Transcript inspected against spoken line, including numeric values and terminology.

en/fa01-03-11.spoken: So the whole tiny cat takes just eight bytes to store.
en/fa01-03-11.previousCheck: Transcript inspected against spoken line, including numeric values and terminology.

en/fa01-04-02.spoken: Let's borrow a very simple idea from a neuron in the brain.
en/fa01-04-02.previousCheck: Transcript inspected against spoken line, including numeric values and terminology.

en/fa01-04-03.spoken: A neuron receives many signals. Some connections have a stronger effect than others.
en/fa01-04-03.previousCheck: Transcript inspected against spoken line, including numeric values and terminology.

en/fa01-04-04.spoken: When the combined input is enough, it sends a signal of its own.
en/fa01-04-04.previousCheck: Transcript inspected against spoken line, including numeric values and terminology.

en/fa01-04-05.spoken: The human brain is often estimated to contain about eighty-six billion neurons.
en/fa01-04-05.previousCheck: Transcript inspected against spoken line, including numeric values and terminology.

en/fa01-04-06.spoken: We can start with a much simpler model, and turn it into a game.
en/fa01-04-06.previousCheck: Transcript inspected against spoken line, including numeric values and terminology.

en/fa01-04-07.spoken: Pretend you are a neuron. Your job is to decide whether something is an apple.
en/fa01-04-07.previousCheck: Transcript inspected against spoken line, including numeric values and terminology.

en/fa01-04-08.spoken: Give it one point for being red, and another point for being round.
en/fa01-04-08.previousCheck: Transcript inspected against spoken line, including numeric values and terminology.

en/fa01-04-09.spoken: When it gets two points, raise your hand. That means you think you found one.
en/fa01-04-09.previousCheck: Transcript inspected against spoken line, including numeric values and terminology.

en/fa01-04-10.spoken: But a tomato can collect both points too. What could you change?
en/fa01-04-10.previousCheck: Transcript inspected against spoken line, including numeric values and terminology.

en/fa01-04-11.spoken: Try another clue: does it taste sweet? How much should that clue count?
en/fa01-04-11.previousCheck: Transcript inspected against spoken line, including numeric values and terminology.

en/fa01-04-12.spoken: Back in nineteen forty nine, Hebb proposed that repeated activity together could strengthen connections.
en/fa01-04-12.previousCheck: Transcript inspected against spoken line, including numeric values and terminology.

en/fa01-05-02.spoken: Every square in the picture has its own points value, ready to be adjusted.
en/fa01-05-02.previousCheck: Transcript inspected against spoken line, including numeric values and terminology.

en/fa01-05-03.spoken: Click Run one round, and watch the points while it works through the examples.
en/fa01-05-03.previousCheck: Transcript inspected against spoken line, including numeric values and terminology.

en/fa01-05-04.spoken: If a horizontal line should switch the light on and does not, add points.
en/fa01-05-04.previousCheck: Transcript inspected against spoken line, including numeric values and terminology.

en/fa01-05-05.spoken: Only change the points for squares that are black in this particular picture.
en/fa01-05-05.previousCheck: Transcript inspected against spoken line, including numeric values and terminology.

en/fa01-05-06.spoken: Look underneath the grid. The numbers in the points list change at the same time.
en/fa01-05-06.previousCheck: Transcript inspected against spoken line, including numeric values and terminology.

en/fa01-05-07.spoken: If the light comes on when it should stay off, lower those points instead.
en/fa01-05-07.previousCheck: Transcript inspected against spoken line, including numeric values and terminology.

en/fa01-05-08.spoken: Now switch to a twenty-by-twenty picture. The learning rule stays just the same.
en/fa01-05-08.previousCheck: Transcript inspected against spoken line, including numeric values and terminology.

en/fa01-05-09.spoken: After training, do the blue points begin to remind you of a seven?
en/fa01-05-09.previousCheck: Transcript inspected against spoken line, including numeric values and terminology.

en/fa01-05-10.spoken: The predict function adds up the points belonging to the black squares.
en/fa01-05-10.previousCheck: Transcript inspected against spoken line, including numeric values and terminology.

en/fa01-05-11.spoken: The train function checks the answer and decides whether those points need changing.
en/fa01-05-11.previousCheck: Transcript inspected against spoken line, including numeric values and terminology.

en/fa01-05-12.spoken: We supply examples and answers. The program adjusts the individual points as it learns.
en/fa01-05-12.previousCheck: Transcript inspected against spoken line, including numeric values and terminology.

en/fa01-06-01.spoken: Now we can reveal X. It is a perceptron.
en/fa01-06-01.previousCheck: Transcript inspected against spoken line, including numeric values and terminology.

en/fa01-06-02.spoken: Frank Rosenblatt described his perceptron ideas in a report published in nineteen fifty seven.
en/fa01-06-02.previousCheck: Transcript inspected against spoken line, including numeric values and terminology.

en/fa01-06-03.spoken: The later Mark one machine had an eye made from a grid of light sensors.
en/fa01-06-03.previousCheck: Transcript inspected against spoken line, including numeric values and terminology.

en/fa01-06-04.spoken: Those sensors were arranged in a twenty-by-twenty array, reading light and dark from a card.
en/fa01-06-04.previousCheck: Transcript inspected against spoken line, including numeric values and terminology.

en/fa01-06-05.spoken: To adjust a connection's strength, a small motor physically turned a potentiometer.
en/fa01-06-05.previousCheck: Transcript inspected against spoken line, including numeric values and terminology.

en/fa01-06-06.spoken: After learning, another card could be presented, and the output indicated the machine's decision.
en/fa01-06-06.previousCheck: Transcript inspected against spoken line, including numeric values and terminology.

en/fa01-06-07.spoken: The positions of those adjustable controls physically stored what the machine had learned.
en/fa01-06-07.previousCheck: Transcript inspected against spoken line, including numeric values and terminology.

en/fa01-06-08.spoken: A nineteen fifty eight newspaper headline described a new Navy device that learns by doing.
en/fa01-06-08.previousCheck: Transcript inspected against spoken line, including numeric values and terminology.

en/fa01-06-09.spoken: This race used a simplified perceptron rule written in JavaScript and running on this Mac.
en/fa01-06-09.previousCheck: Second take clearly says this race; transcript matches.

en/fa01-06-10.spoken: It had already learned from four hundred and nineteen training pictures before entering the race.
en/fa01-06-10.previousCheck: Transcript inspected against spoken line, including numeric values and terminology.

en/fa01-07-01.spoken: Why was it so fast? Now we can look at how much work it actually does.
en/fa01-07-01.previousCheck: Transcript inspected against spoken line, including numeric values and terminology.

en/fa01-07-02.spoken: For one picture, it needs at most four hundred additions to collect the points.
en/fa01-07-02.previousCheck: Transcript inspected against spoken line, including numeric values and terminology.

en/fa01-07-03.spoken: The local Qwen model has roughly eight billion parameters, a much larger collection of numbers.
en/fa01-07-03.previousCheck: Transcript inspected against spoken line, including numeric values and terminology.

en/fa01-07-04.spoken: It calculates across many layers, then writes its answer one token at a time.
en/fa01-07-04.previousCheck: Second take clearly says across many layers; transcript matches.

en/fa01-07-05.spoken: This simple artificial neuron was part of a much longer story of increasingly complex networks.
en/fa01-07-05.previousCheck: Transcript inspected against spoken line, including numeric values and terminology.

en/fa01-07-06.spoken: In nineteen sixty nine, Minsky and Papert published a detailed mathematical study of perceptrons and their limitations.
en/fa01-07-06.previousCheck: Transcript inspected against spoken line, including numeric values and terminology.

en/fa01-07-07.spoken: Interest later cooled for a time. Backpropagation helped make networks with multiple layers learn effectively.
en/fa01-07-07.previousCheck: Transcript inspected against spoken line, including numeric values and terminology.

en/fa01-07-08.spoken: In twenty twelve, a deep neural network made a major breakthrough in the ImageNet picture-recognition competition.
en/fa01-07-08.previousCheck: Transcript inspected against spoken line, including numeric values and terminology.

en/fa01-07-10.spoken: Those models can discuss far more than this one small question about a picture.
en/fa01-07-10.previousCheck: Transcript inspected against spoken line, including numeric values and terminology.

en/fa01-07-11.spoken: Even a simple request can still require a great deal of computation.
en/fa01-07-11.previousCheck: Transcript inspected against spoken line, including numeric values and terminology.

en/fa01-08-01.spoken: You can begin exploring these ideas right at your own family table.
en/fa01-08-01.previousCheck: Transcript inspected against spoken line, including numeric values and terminology.

en/fa01-08-02.spoken: Print a worksheet, find a few pencils, and leave some room for trying things out.
en/fa01-08-02.previousCheck: Transcript inspected against spoken line, including numeric values and terminology.

en/fa01-08-03.spoken: One person reads the numbers, while someone else colors in the hidden picture.
en/fa01-08-03.previousCheck: Transcript inspected against spoken line, including numeric values and terminology.

en/fa01-08-04.spoken: Then take turns being the neuron. Decide together how much each clue should count.
en/fa01-08-04.previousCheck: Transcript inspected against spoken line, including numeric values and terminology.

en/fa01-08-05.spoken: When you want the computer to try, open the browser lab and teach it with examples.
en/fa01-08-05.previousCheck: Transcript inspected against spoken line, including numeric values and terminology.

en/fa01-08-06.spoken: Scan the code to open the lab and find the printable worksheets.
en/fa01-08-06.previousCheck: Transcript inspected against spoken line, including numeric values and terminology.
